newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurds extend U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds extend U.S.-brokered ceasefire.

text.p: Feuding Iraqi Kurdish factions on Thursday agreed to extend permanently a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that ended two months of clashes in northern Iraq last week, U.S. peace envoy Robert Pelletreau said.

"All participants agree to maintain and strengthen the ceasefire within a permament context," Pelletreau told a news conference after two days of talks with the two Kurdish groups in the Turkish capital.
Pelletreau brokered a ceasefire between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) last week.
The clashes gave President Saddam Hussein a foothold in Western-protected northern Iraq after a five-year break.
The KDP joined forces with Baghdad in late August to take the key city of Arbil from the PUK, prompting U.S. missile strikes against targets in southern Iraq.
The KDP accuses Iran of backing the PUK militarily. Both the PUK and Tehran deny this.

Pelletreau, the assistant secretary of state for near eastern affairs, said the Kurds had also agreed "to reestablish peace and stability in northern Iraq by beginning a process of political" reconcilitation.
The two groups are to meet again in Ankara on November 15, he said.
Washington brought the factions to two rounds of peace talks in Ireland after fighting last year but no concrete settlement to their power struggle was reached.
